course.programmeTitle: Bachelor of Engineering in Data Science and Engineering
course.title: Predictive Analytics
course.prerequisites: Math I–III; Statistics I–II; Advanced Programming (Python & OOP); Data Manipulation and Visualization
course.description: Predictive Analytics introduces students to techniques used to analyze historical data and build predictive models for decision making. The course focuses on practical skills in data preparation, exploratory data analysis, feature engineering, and predictive modeling using Python. Students will learn how to implement predictive analytics workflows using common data science tools such as Pandas, NumPy, Matplotlib, and Scikit-learn. The course covers regression models, classification models, and model evaluation techniques including Mean Squared Error (MSE), Accuracy, Precision, Recall, and ROC/AUC. A project-based learning approach is emphasized throughout the semester. Students progressively develop a mini predictive analytics project using real-world datasets from Kaggle, allowing them to experience the full data science workflow from data preprocessing to model evaluation and communication of analytical findings. By the end of the course, students will be able to build predictive models, evaluate their performance, and communicate insights derived from data effectively.

clos.description: Produce exploratory data reports and well-structured, cleaned datasets suitable for predictive modelling tasks.
clos.teachingMethodsRaw: Lecture + Guided Hands-on Lab + Demonstration (Python, EDA)

clos.description: Construct modular and reusable machine learning pipelines to automate data processing and model workflows.
clos.teachingMethodsRaw: Lab-based Learning + Step-by-step Coding + Scaffolded Exercises (Pipeline building)

clos.description: Justify the selection of appropriate models and evaluation metrics based on problem requirements and performance results.
clos.teachingMethodsRaw: Case Study + Model Comparison + Discussion + Problem-based Learning
clos.assessmentMethodsRaw: Final Report & Kaggle Submission (Model Justification & Evaluation)

clos.description: Organize a collaborative project using professional tools, demonstrating effective teamwork and communication.
clos.teachingMethodsRaw: Team-based Learning + Project-based Learning + Presentation Coaching

topics.title: Topic 1: Intro to Predictive Analytics
topics.llosRaw: LLO1: Differentiate supervised vs unsupervised learning. LLO2: Explain ML workflow. LLO3: Setup Python environment for data science.

topics.title: Topic 2: Python for Data Science (NumPy & Pandas)
topics.llosRaw: LLO1: Apply NumPy operations. LLO2: Use Pandas to explore datasets. LLO3: Configure Kaggle and download datasets.

topics.title: Topic 3: Exploratory Data Analysis (EDA)
topics.llosRaw: LLO1: Detect missing values and outliers. LLO2: Visualize distributions and correlations.

topics.title: Topic 4: Data Cleaning & Preprocessing
topics.llosRaw: LLO1: Handle missing values. LLO2: Encode categorical variables. LLO3: Split dataset into train/test sets.

topics.title: Topic 5: Baseline Model Development
topics.llosRaw: LLO1: Build initial ML models. LLO2: Evaluate model performance.

topics.title: Topic 6: Feature Engineering
topics.llosRaw: LLO1: Transform and scale features. LLO2: Generate new features.

topics.title: Topic 7: Machine Learning Pipeline
topics.llosRaw: LLO1: Build modular ML workflows. LLO2: Combine preprocessing and modelling. LLO3: Reuse pipelines for experiments.

topics.title: Topic 8: Regression Models
topics.llosRaw: LLO1: Train regression models. LLO2: Evaluate using RMSE/MAE.

topics.title: Topic 9: Classification Models
topics.llosRaw: LLO1: Train classification models. LLO2: Evaluate Accuracy/F1/ROC-AUC.

topics.title: Topic 10: Model Evaluation
topics.llosRaw: LLO1: Analyse model performance metrics. LLO2: Visualize confusion matrices/ROC curves.

topics.title: Topic 11: Model Tuning & Hyperparameters
topics.llosRaw: LLO1: Optimize models with GridSearchCV. LLO2: Improve metrics; balance bias-variance trade-off.

topics.title: Topic 12: Team Project Planning
topics.llosRaw: LLO1: Define dataset, KPIs, and team roles. LLO2: Use Notion/Trello to plan workflow.

topics.title: Topic 13: Team Model Development & Comparison
topics.llosRaw: LLO1: Build collaborative pipelines LLO2: Compare models; generate leaderboard-ready submission

topics.title: Topic 14: Data Storytelling & Presentation
topics.llosRaw: LLO1: Communicate model results LLO2: Explain business impact

studentResponsibilitiesRaw: Read the learning materials beforehand which means to be ready for the next session. Be completely engaged in class, active, take notes, and ask questions in class. Students are required to participate in various activities in and out of the classroom, such as group work, and individual homework for assignments and reports assigned by the subject teacher. Submit the assigned tasks such as homework, assignments, or research proposal on time.
coursePolicyRaw: Attendance & Preparation Students are expected to attend all classes (online/on-site). Assigned readings and preparation outlines must be completed before class if any. Active participation in group discussions and post-chapter evaluations is required. Academic Integrity All assignments, quizzes, and exams must be done individually. Academic misconduct includes: - Presenting others’ work as one’s own. - Engaging in plagiarism or cheating. Homework & Assignments Preparation outlines must be submitted on time; late submissions incur penalties. Peer discussion is encouraged, but midterm and final exams must be independent. Examinations Midterm and final exams are closed-book. Penalties Violations of academic integrity may result in a failing grade and referral to the Office of Student Affairs. Students uncertain about potential violations should consult the instructor in advance.
